name: field-service
description: A multi-tenant field-service dispatch backend: shared region reference data, per-tenant customers, and per-tenant work orders assigned to technicians. Every construct here exists so one end-to-end test can measure one behaviour F3 claims — see README.md for the construct-to-behaviour table.

work-order-ref.description: The letters WO, a dash, then four to eight digits. Written without ^...$ on purpose: Alvo anchors a format over the whole value, so a value with trailing text is refused by the framework's anchoring rather than by the author's.

regions.description: A service region. Shared reference data (a ciselnik): global rather than tenant-scoped, so every tenant reads the same rows.

code.description: The region's short code, unique across the instance.

customers.description: A customer of one tenant. Deliberately NOT audited, so its rows carry no version: no ETag is minted for one and an If-Match naming a version is refused rather than ignored.

tier.description: Which service tier the customer is on.

work_orders.description: One job to be carried out for a customer, in a region, by a technician. Audited, so every row carries a version and every write of one can be made conditional.

reference.description: The human-facing work-order reference, unique within the instance.

description.description: The full job description as the customer gave it.

status.description: Where the job is in its life cycle.

priority.description: Dispatch priority, 1 (highest) to 5 (lowest). Required, so a paged read may sort by it.

quoted_price.description: What the customer was quoted, excluding tax.

is_emergency.description: Whether the job was raised as an emergency call-out.

scheduled_for.description: When the technician is due on site. Nullable, so a paged read may NOT sort by it.

completed_on.description: The day the job was signed off, if it has been.

contact_email.description: Who to tell when the job is done.

metadata.description: Whatever the dispatch system attached to the job.

assigned_to.description: The user id of the technician the job is assigned to. The rules below compare it with @user.id, which is what makes a technician's list a subset rather than a refusal.

external_ref.description: The identifier this job carries in the customer's own system. Maintained by the integration, never by an API caller.

internal_notes.description: Dispatcher-only commentary. Confidential: neither the value nor the fact that this field exists may reach a caller, so it appears in no response and in no published schema.

access_code.description: The site access code the caller must supply on create and can never read back. Required AND hidden, which is the one case a hidden field's name is published — in the write schemas only.

customer_id.description: The customer this job is for.

region_id.description: The region the job is carried out in.
